description:
crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:159-198 — now_utc_string returns a
jmap_types::UTCDate whose underlying string is the 24-character
"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ" form (with millisecond fraction).

jmap-types/src/id.rs:404-407 shows UTCDate::new_validated rejects this
form:

    fn utcdate_new_validated_wrong_length_fails() {
        assert!(UTCDate::new_validated("2014-10-30").is_err());
        // ↓ This is the same shape now_utc_string emits today:
        assert!(UTCDate::new_validated("2014-10-30T06:12:00.000Z").is_err());
    }

The function doc (helpers.rs:131-137) acknowledges this:

> The string the UTCDate wraps does not pass UTCDate::new_validated
> because that validator requires exactly the 20-char
> YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ form (no millis) and this helper emits the
> 24-char form with millis. The workspace convention is to use the
> 24-char form on the wire — consumers wanting strict validation
> should construct their own UTCDate::new_validated value from a
> chrono-formatted source.

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That UTCDate values produced by jmap-server pass UTCDate's own
   validator. The newtype's name and dedicated `new_validated`
   constructor strongly imply "this type's instances are validated";
   today they are not.

2. That a future contributor who tightens UTCDate to enforce its
   invariant won't break every now_utc_string call site. Right
   now, the only thing preventing a UTCDate(String) from being
   malformed is the absence of validation on the unsafe-ish
   `UTCDate::from(impl Into<String>)` constructor.

3. That RFC 8620 §1.4 conformance is what UTCDate guarantees.
   RFC 8620 §1.4 explicitly permits both the 20-char and the
   millisecond-fraction form; UTCDate::new_validated is stricter
   than the RFC. This is a jmap-types problem, but it surfaces
   through now_utc_string here.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

- A consumer writes a contract test asserting `for every UTCDate
  the kit emits, UTCDate::new_validated(d.as_ref()).is_ok()` and
  it fails. They file a bug against jmap-server.
- A future hardening pass on jmap-types tightens the `From<&str>`
  impl to validate; every now_utc_string call site newly produces
  invalid values and the wire format breaks.
- Type-level guarantees are weaker than they appear — the
  `new_validated` naming convention is broken in spirit.

Resolution paths (one is sufficient):

- Update UTCDate::new_validated in jmap-types to accept both the
  20-char and 24-char forms per RFC 8620 §1.4. This is the
  spec-faithful fix; now_utc_string then produces validated values.
  Workspace-impact: medium — touches jmap-types and adds two test
  cases.

- Rename now_utc_string to make the contract clear:
  `now_utc_date_with_millis() -> UTCDate` — but the name still
  invokes UTCDate, so this only partially helps.

- Add a `UTCDate::from_str_lax(&str)` constructor that explicitly
  accepts both forms, and have now_utc_string use it. Tightens the
  type's API surface.

- Document the discrepancy on UTCDate's own type doc, not just on
  now_utc_string's function doc, so consumers reading UTCDate's
  docs know the invariant is not enforced.

The current state is a docs-only contract crack between two
adjacent crates. Closing it makes the type story honest.
title: now_utc_string returns UTCDate but value fails UTCDate::new_validated — newtype invariant silently broken
